findings.title: LLM endpoint with no visible rate limiting
findings.fix: Rate-limit every LLM endpoint (per user and per IP) and cap tokens per request. With Fastify: await fastify.register(import("@fastify/rate-limit"), { max: 20, timeWindow: "1 minute" }); with Next.js: add a rate-limit check in middleware or in the handler before calling the model.

findings.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML with untrusted input
findings.fix: Avoid dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Render the content as React children, or sanitise it first with a library such as DOMPurify and only then inject it.

findings.title: SQL built by string concatenation or template interpolation
findings.fix: Use parameterised queries (placeholders) instead of building SQL from strings. Example: db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1", [userId])

findings.title: Sensitive data written to console logs
findings.evidence: console.log('Login attempt for', email, 'with password', password)
findings.fix: Remove the log line, or log only a redacted value (e.g. the last 4 characters of a token). Logs are often shipped to third-party services.

findings.title: Hardcoded secret or API key
findings.fix: Move the value into an environment variable and read it with process.env. Never commit real credentials. Example: const apiKey = process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY; if (!apiKey) throw new Error("OPENAI_API_KEY is not set");

findings.title: eval() or new Function() with dynamic code
findings.fix: Remove eval / new Function. Use JSON.parse for data, a map of allowed functions for behaviour, or a proper expression parser.

findings.title: Route handler with no visible auth check
findings.fix: Check authentication before doing anything sensitive, in the handler, in middleware.ts, or in a Fastify preHandler hook. Example (Next.js): const session = await getServerSession(authOptions); if (!session) return Response.json({ error: "Unauthorized" }, { status: 401 });

findings.title: Route handler with no visible input validation
findings.fix: Validate input before using it. With Zod: const body = schema.parse(await req.json()); with Fastify: add a schema option to the route. Return 400 with a consistent error shape on invalid input.

findings.title: CORS allows any origin with credentials
findings.fix: Restrict CORS to your own origins: origin: ["https://app.example.com"]. Never use origin: "*" together with credentials: true.

findings.title: Fastify route without schema validation
findings.evidence: fastify.post('/login', async (req, reply) => {   const { email, password } = req.body;   c
findings.fix: Add a schema option to the route: fastify.post("/users", { schema: { body: { type: "object", required: ["email"], properties: { email: { type: "string", format: "email" } } } } }, handler)

findings.title: JWT signed or verified with a hardcoded secret
findings.fix: Read the JWT secret from the environment: jwt.sign(payload, process.env.JWT_SECRET). Use a long random secret (32+ characters) and rotate it if it was ever committed.

findings.evidence: for (const id of ids) { const user = await

findings.title: Raw tag instead of next/image
findings.fix: Use next/image for automatic optimisation: import Image from "next/image"; <Image src={...} alt="..." width={800} height={600} />

findings.title: Fastify server without compression
findings.fix: Register compression: await fastify.register(import("@fastify/compress"));

findings.title: Error response may leak internals
findings.fix: Return a generic error message to the client and log the details server-side. Example: return Response.json({ error: "Internal server error" }, { status: 500 });
